results.claim: When k=2, a vertex is uniquely determined by its support.
results.proof_sketch: Every nonnegative integer vector of coordinate sum two is either 2e_i, with singleton support {i}, or e_i+e_j for distinct i,j, with support {i,j}. Thus recovering the support recovers the vertex.

results.claim: For k=2 and distinct a,b, the landmark e_a+e_b measures the sum of the support indicators at a and b.
results.proof_sketch: The source distance formula gives d(x,r)=2−Σ_i min(x_i,r_i), since both coordinate sums are two. Consequently, 2−d(x,e_a+e_b)=1_{x_a>0}+1_{x_b>0}.

results.claim: On a block consisting of one center and at least three leaves, the center–leaf landmarks recover every support of size at most two within that block.
results.proof_sketch: Let L≥3 be the number of leaves, let u_j be their standard basis vectors, and write 1 for the all-ones vector of length L. The overlap vectors for the possible supports are: 0 for the empty support; u_j for one leaf; 1 for the center; u_j+u_l for two distinct leaves; and 1+u_j for the center and one leaf. These vectors are pairwise distinct. In particular, 1 has at least three nonzero coordinates, while supports without the center yield at most two nonzero coordinates; a center–leaf pair produces an entry equal to two.

Set q=⌊n/4⌋. Partition the coordinates into q blocks, each of size at least four: use q−1 blocks of size four and one block of size 4+(n mod 4). In each block choose a center and take all center–leaf vertices as landmarks. There are Σ_blocks(|block|−1)=n−q landmarks. Their distances recover the support within every block by the preceding claim. They therefore recover the global support and hence every vertex.

results.claim: For n=8 and k=2, six explicit admissible landmarks resolve all 36 vertices.
results.proof_sketch: Take R={e_1+e_2,e_1+e_3,e_1+e_4,e_5+e_6,e_5+e_7,e_5+e_8}. These are six distinct nonnegative integer vectors of length eight and coordinate sum two. They form the star construction on blocks {1,2,3,4} and {5,6,7,8}, so their distance vectors recover every vertex. The complete vertex set has binomial(9,2)=36 elements. The saved exact checker independently confirms 36 distinct signatures.

results.claim: Represent any resolving set R for k=2 by a simple graph H of pair landmarks and a marked set M of double landmarks. If H has an unmarked isolated vertex, then |R|≥n−1.
results.proof_sketch: Put ij in E(H) exactly when e_i+e_j belongs to R, and put i in M exactly when 2e_i belongs to R. Suppose i is isolated and unmarked. If another vertex j were unmarked, then 2e_j and e_i+e_j would have identical distances to every landmark. Pair landmarks contain no i and have the same overlap with both vertices. Double landmarks are at coordinates outside {i,j} and have overlap zero with both. Therefore every j≠i must be marked, giving |R|≥|M|≥n−1.

results.claim: An unmarked tree component of H cannot have two or three vertices when R resolves F_2(K_n).
results.proof_sketch: For a two-vertex component with edge ij, the vertices 2e_i and 2e_j have overlap one with its sole landmark and overlap zero with all other landmarks. They are indistinguishable. A three-vertex tree is a path a−b−c. The vertices 2e_b and e_a+e_c both have overlap one with each of its two edge landmarks and overlap zero with all remaining landmarks. They are again indistinguishable. These collisions contradict resolution.

results.claim: For every n≥4, every resolving set for F_2(K_n) has at least n−⌊n/4⌋ landmarks.
results.proof_sketch: Use H and M as above, so |R|=|E(H)|+|M|. If an unmarked isolated vertex exists, the preceding bound gives |R|≥n−1≥n−⌊n/4⌋. Otherwise, every unmarked tree component has at least four vertices. Let t be the number of these components; then t≤⌊n/4⌋. A component with v vertices and a mark contributes at least (v−1)+1=v landmarks. An unmarked component containing a cycle contributes at least v edges. Each unmarked tree contributes v−1 edges. Summing over all components yields |R|≥n−t≥n−⌊n/4⌋.

results.claim: For every n≥4, dim(F_2(K_n))=n−⌊n/4⌋; in particular, dim(F_2(K_8))=6.
results.proof_sketch: The star construction supplies the upper bound and the component argument supplies the matching lower bound. At n=8 the common value is 8−2=6. Independently, exhaustive enumeration in the saved checker rules out all 376,992 five-landmark subsets of the 36 vertices. Every smaller resolving set could be extended to five landmarks, so this enumeration also certifies the lower bound six.

The conjecture quantifies over all integers n≥1 and k≥1. The admissible instance n=8,k=2 has metric dimension six, whereas its asserted value is n−1=7. Thus this instance refutes the original universal assertion. The general k=2 formula additionally contradicts it for every n≥8.

final_writeup:
The conjecture is refuted: dim(F_2(K_8))=6, whereas the asserted value is seven.

Let e_i denote the ith standard basis vector in eight coordinates. Take

R={e_1+e_2, e_1+e_3, e_1+e_4, e_5+e_6, e_5+e_7, e_5+e_8}.

The parameters n=8 and k=2 satisfy the stated domain. Every element of R is a distinct nonnegative integer vector with coordinate sum two, so R is an admissible six-vertex landmark set in the exact graph specified by the source.

Here is a complete certificate that R resolves every vertex. Write s_i=1 when x_i>0 and s_i=0 otherwise. The given distance formula implies

2−d(x,e_a+e_b)=s_a+s_b.

For a four-coordinate block with center a and leaves b,c,d, the three landmarks therefore reveal (s_a+s_b,s_a+s_c,s_a+s_d). Because x has only two tokens, its support within this block has size at most two. The possible supports and overlap vectors are

∅→000; {a}→111; {b}→100; {c}→010; {d}→001; {a,b}→211; {a,c}→121; {a,d}→112; {b,c}→110; {b,d}→101; {c,d}→011.

All eleven vectors are distinct. Applying this decoding to blocks {1,2,3,4} and {5,6,7,8} recovers the entire support. A singleton support {i} forces x=2e_i, and a two-element support {i,j} forces x=e_i+e_j. Hence every pair of distinct vertices has different distance vectors to R. Therefore dim(F_2(K_8))≤6<7, which already completely refutes the conjecture.

The construction also gives the exact formula dim(F_2(K_n))=n−⌊n/4⌋ for every n≥4. For the upper bound, partition the coordinates into ⌊n/4⌋ blocks of size at least four and use all center–leaf landmarks within each block. The same decoding works with any number of leaves at least three.

For the lower bound, encode an arbitrary resolving set by a graph H whose edges represent landmarks e_i+e_j, marking coordinate i when 2e_i is a landmark. An unmarked isolated coordinate forces every other coordinate to be marked: otherwise 2e_j and e_i+e_j are indistinguishable. This case requires at least n−1 landmarks. In the remaining case, unmarked tree components have at least four vertices. A two-vertex component cannot distinguish its two doubled endpoints; a three-vertex path cannot distinguish its doubled center from its two occupied leaves. Each marked component or cyclic component contributes at least as many landmarks as vertices. Each unmarked tree component saves only one landmark and uses at least four vertices. Thus there are at most ⌊n/4⌋ such savings, proving the matching lower bound.

Its computations use only integers and the Python standard library.
